_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce recurrence of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) in adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older who are receiving antibacterial drug treatment for CDI and are at a high risk for CDI recurrence; not indicated for the treatment of CDI.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (adaptive design, four arms: actoxumab+bezlotoxumab, actoxumab, bezlotoxumab, placebo), all with standard of care antibacterial drugs.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age or older receiving standard-of-care antibacterial drugs (metronidazole, vancomycin, or fidaxomicin) for an episode of CDI.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects in the Full Analysis Set with CDI recurrence during the 12-week (Day 85 ± 5 days) follow-up period after infusion of study drug.
pivotal_trials.n: 1452 randomized; FAS 1396 (383 actoxumab+bezlotoxumab, 232 actoxumab, 386 bezlotoxumab, 395 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: CDI recurrence (bezlotoxumab vs placebo): 17.4% (67/386) vs 27.6% (109/395); adjusted difference -10.1% (95% CI -15.9, -4.3), p=0.0006.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with three arms (actoxumab+bezlotoxumab, bezlotoxumab, placebo), all with standard of care antibacterial drugs.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age or older receiving standard-of-care antibacterial drugs (metronidazole, vancomycin, or fidaxomicin) for an episode of CDI.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects in the Full Analysis Set with CDI recurrence during the 12-week (Day 85 ± 5 days) follow-up period after infusion of study drug.
pivotal_trials.result: CDI recurrence (bezlotoxumab vs placebo): 15.7% (62/395) vs 25.7% (97/378); adjusted difference -9.9% (95% CI -15.5, -4.2), p=0.0006.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in adults (≥4% and greater than placebo, within 4 weeks): nausea (7% vs 5%), pyrexia (5% vs 3%), and headache (4% vs 3%). Heart failure was reported more commonly in ZINPLAVA-treated patients with a history of CHF (serious heart failure in 12.7% [15/118] vs 4.8% [5/104] placebo).
target_moa: Bezlotoxumab is a human monoclonal IgG1 antibody that binds to C. difficile toxin B and neutralizes its effects, inhibiting binding of toxin B and preventing its effects on mammalian cells; it does not bind toxin A.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory committee held June 9, 2016; asked whether the Applicant provided substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness of bezlotoxumab for prevention of CDI recurrence: 10 yes, 5 no, 1 abstention.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients 1 year to less than 18 years of age to reduce recurrence of C. difficile infection

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for the expansion of the use of Zinplava injection to reduce recurrence of *Clostridioides difficile* infection (CDI) in patients who are receiving antibacterial drug treatment for CDI and are at a high risk for CDI recurrence to include pediatric patients 1 year to less than 18 years of age, based on the completion of post-marketing requirement (PMR) 3118-1, listed in the October 21, 2016, approval letter.

The response to this request constituted a major amendment to the BLA necessitating the extension of the review clock. On June 30, 2016 the major amendment was received and the review goal date was extended by 3 months. The results of the analyses of Phase 3 trials are the main subject of this review.

The advisory committee for this BLA took place on June 9, 2016. The committee was asked whether the Applicant provided substantial evidence of the safety and effectiveness of bezlotoxumab for the prevention of C. difficile infection recurrence. There were 10 yes votes, 5 no and 1 abstention.

requirement.text: 3118-1: Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of Zinplava in pediatric patients from 1 to less than 18 years of age receiving antibacterial therapy for C. difficile infection (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: **3118-1:** Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of Zinplava (bezlotoxumab) in pediatric patients from 1 to less than 18 years of age receiving antibacterial therapy for *C. difficile* infection.

requirement.text: 3118-2: Perform low endotoxin recovery studies, using an endotoxin standard as the spiking material.

citations.quote:

Use an endotoxin standard as the spiking material.

requirement.text: 3118-3: Repeat the microbial retention study using a more suitable surrogate solution modeling the drug product.

citations.quote: **3118-3:** Repeat the microbial retention study using a more suitable surrogate solution. Attributes of the surrogate solution that are known to affect microbial retention (surface tension, viscosity, ionic strength, etc.) should model the drug product as closely as possible while preserving viability of the challenge organism. Alternatively, use of a reduced exposure time or modified process conditions (e.g., temperature) may be appropriate. Provide the summary data, the associated report, and justification for any modifications to the study. If any (b) (4) parameters are changed as a result of the study, update the BLA file accordingly.

requirement.text: 3118-5: Conduct a study to support the worst case cumulative hold times in the bezlotoxumab drug substance manufacturing process.

citations.quote: **3118-5:** Conduct a study to support the worst case cumulative hold times in the bezlotomumab drug substance manufacturing process to demonstrate that the worst case cumulative hold time will not adversely affect the product quality of bezlotomumab drug substance. These data are expected to demonstrate that there is no adverse impact to product quality (b) (4)

requirement.text: 3118-6: Develop a valid in vitro endotoxin assay for drug product release testing.

citations.quote: **3118-6:** Develop a valid *in vitro* endotoxin assay for drug product release testing. Conduct studies to evaluate sample preparation, sample pre-treatment, and alternative test methods for endotoxin detection.

requirement.text: 3118-7: Re-evaluate MK-6072 drug substance and drug product lot release and stability specifications after a minimum of 30 DS lots have been manufactured.

citations.quote: **3118-7:** Re-evaluate MK-6072 drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) lot release and stability specifications after a minimum of 30 DS lots have been manufactured using the commercial manufacturing process and tested at the time of release using the commercial specification methods. The corresponding data, the analytical and statistical plan used to evaluate the specifications, and any proposed changes to the specifications will be provided in the final study report.
